newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin flies to Helsinki for tough summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin flies to Helsinki for tough summit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin left for Helsinki on Thursday for a summit meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton billed as the toughest since the end of the Cold War.

Television footage showed Yeltsin dressed in a long dark coat mounting the steps of his brand-new presidential plane at the Vnukovo-2 government airport in a flurry of snow. He was accompanied by his wife Naina.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and other officials saw Yeltsin off at the airport.
The president, firmly back at the helm after months of illness, strode confidently up the steps of the Ilyushin Il-96, which set off for the Finnish capital just after 2 p.m. (1100 GMT).
The thorny issue of NATO expansion is expected to top the summit's agenda, which will also include Russia's economic reforms and arms control.

Russian officials have stepped up their verbal offensive against NATO's plans on the eve of the summit, saying they were the West's biggest mistake since the end of the Cold War. Moscow regards NATO's intention to admit former communist countries in eastern and central Europe as a threat to its own security.
Kremlin press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Thursday in Helsinki that Yeltsin would defend Moscow's interests "like never before" during the summit talks.
He also warned that NATO's plans could force Russia to review its foreign policy and strengthen links with countries like China, India and Iran.

Washington and its allies have made clear that they will press on with NATO expansion despite Russian objections but are offering Moscow a new partnership through a charter that would give Russia a say in European security issues.

Yeltsin and Clinton, who arrived in Helsinki earlier on Thursday, were meeting on Thursday evening at a dinner hosted by Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari. Their main talks start on Friday morning. Yeltsin returns to Moscow on Saturday.
